newsitem.title: USA: First Merchants restating 96, sees Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: First Merchants restating 96, sees Q1 loss.

text.p: First Merchants Acceptance Corp said Tuesday that it would restate its 1996 results after discovering "irregularities involving unauthorized entries" in its financial records.
Additionally, the company said it is delaying its first quarter results and expects to report a loss of between $1.60 and $2 a share for the quarter.
"This is primarily because of a significant increase in the provision for credit losses reflecting changes in management's estimates of projected required reserves," the company said in a release.
Shares of First Merchants, a company engaged mainly in financing purchases of used automobiles, closed off 3/8 Tuesday at 6-5/8.

As a result of the discovered irregularities, the Deerfield, Illinois-based company said it was out of compliance with certain covenants under its financing arrangements, though it had made all payments on a timely basis and is talking to its lenders.
"The company believes that its financial condition remains strong and will support its continuing operations and plans for future growth," the company's release said.
The company said its board terminated the employment of four employees, including its president and chief executive, Mitchell Kahn.
Attempts to reach company officials and Kahn on Tuesday evening were not immediately successful.
The company said its new chief financial officer, Norman Smagley, was conducting an investigation with outside counsel and independent auditors. The company did not identify Smagley's predecessor.
It said it had begun searching for a new chief executive and that it has appointed two directors to serve as co-chief executive officers on an interim basis.
The company said it expected its restated 1996 earnings would amount to at least $1 a share. The company had originally reported 1996 earnings of $1.56 a share.
The company said its restated 1996 and first-quarter results should be available in early May.
